title: Neuro-Symbolic AI for Analytical Solutions of Differential Equations
claim: A grammar-generated function library is embedded into a continuous latent space, then searched in two stages to find closed-form solutions.
layout: 4 stacked panels A–D, top-to-bottom, arrows between steps, latent manifold surfaces
description: Four stacked rounded panels labeled A–D read top to bottom and walk through the method. A, 'Grammar and Language', shows a circle of terminal symbols, the grammar tuple and production rules in the middle, and a circle of example expressions such as sin(x/t) and log(x) on the right. B, 'Language of Functions', shows an expression tree for exp(-t)sin(10t) and its token sequence. An arrow labeled I leads to a blue function-space surface with dots and a small damped-oscillation plot. C, 'Autoencoding', shows an encoder arrow into a gray latent patch with contour ellipses, then a decoder arrow back to the blue surface with clustered dots. D, 'Solution Search', shows structure discovery as purple and blue paths over the latent patch, and coefficient refinement as an argmin formula. Purple accents mark the selected expression and its latent point.
caption: Overview over the proposed Symbolic Iterative Grammar Solver (SIGS). A. Terminal symbols Φ and rules R, together with non-terminals N and starting symbol S, form the grammar G which generates the mathematical expressions in the library L(G). B. Each expression w ∈L(G) is identified with a function u in the finite set of candidate functions U. C. The encoder E and decoder D of the Grammar Variational Autoencoder (GVAE, (Kusner et al., 2017)) embed the finite L(G) into the continuous latent space Z. D. Given a differential equation and system conditions, a structure search is performed over z ∈Z using iterative clustering, followed by a separate optimization of the constants in the final structure, optimizing for lowest residual R of the corresponding candidate function u = (I ◦D)(z) ∈U.
abstract: Analytical solutions to differential equations offer exact, interpretable insight but are rarely available because discovering them requires expert intuition or exhaustive search of combinatorial spaces. We introduce SIGS, a neuro-symbolic framework for equation-driven closed-form solution discovery. SIGS uses a context-free grammar to generate mathematically valid and physically meaningful building blocks, with a user-specified Ansatz prescribing how these blocks combine, embeds them into a topology-regularised continuous latent manifold, and searches this manifold in two stages: structure selection followed by coefficient refinement using gradient descent, scoring candidates only against the PDE residual and prescribed boundary and initial conditions. This design unifies symbolic reasoning with numerical optimization; the grammar constrains candidate solution blocks to be proper by construction, while the latent search makes exploration tractable and data-free. SIGS is the first neuro-symbolic method to (i) recover analytical solutions for coupled nonlinear PDE systems, (ii) discover equivalent symbolic forms when the grammar lacks the natural primitives, and (iii) produce accurate symbolic approximations for PDEs lacking known closed-form solutions. Overall, SIGS improves over existing symbolic methods by orders of magnitude in both accuracy and runtime across standard PDE benchmarks.
